articles.title: Scott Jennings humiliated as CNN panel laughs at his 'comedic' Trump hypothetical
articles.description: Conservative CNN pundit Scott Jennings botched an attempt to defend President Donald Trump's tariffs with a hypothetical that led to everyone laughing in his face. On Wednesday, Jennings was part of the roundtable on CNN Newsnight, and he tried to back up Trump's handling of the economy by posing a question to the other pundits, including former New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio , New York Times reporter Lulu Garcia-Navarro and Democratic political strategist Bakari Sellers. "I have a sincere question for you because you all very concerned about the tariffs as taxes," Jennings said, referring to critics' argument that tariffs function as a tax on American consumers because importers pass the cost along as higher prices. "If Donald Trump tomorrow said, 'I'll trade you elimination of all tariffs for elimination of all corporate income taxes,' would you take the deal?" The panel responded with faces of confusion. De Blasio squinted his eyes and turned his head sideways while Garcia-Navarro threw her hands up and stared blankly at Jennings. No one responded for several seconds until host Abby Phillip asked, "What is that, Scott?" "Would you take all taxes down to zero?" Jennings asked. De Blasio, still squinting, shook his head and said, "No," while Garcia-Navarro waved the question away. "What is the point of that hypothetical, Scott?" Phillip asked. As Jennings took himself seriously, everyone else at the table began cracking up as he tried to explain, "The point is this, because you're mad about certain taxes, but every Democrat constantly argues for tax increases on corporations against tariffs. It makes no sense." "Scott, you're the conservative at this table. That's why this is so comedic," Phillip explained while Jennings, with an angry expression, turned to Sellers, who was laughing with the other pundits still, and yelled, "Do you not understand this? It's a very simple argument!" "You have to bend over backwards to explain the conservative rationale for tariffs, and I don't see you doing it," Phillip said. "You keep telling me this is what Trump believes."

articles.title: U.S. Postal Service Chief Is Reportedly So Fed Up He Wants to Quit
articles.description: Postmaster General David Steiner wants out. The United States Postal Service chief told individuals close to him that he wants to resign from his post, according to a report from Reuters on Wednesday. “The message was, this isn’t what he signed up for, and he didn’t come on board to get beat up like this,” one source said. This report comes as President Trump has been attempting to use the supposedly independent mail service to do his bidding in his last-minute midterm election interference, commanding it to only deliver ballots if they had a unique barcode and if states handed over voter lists to the agency. The Supreme Court struck that dream down on Monday, just two days before reports of Steiner’s discontent. USPS has denied the report, saying it has “absolutely zero ⁠validity.” Steiner was apparently most discouraged after an intense Senate hearing earlier this summer in which he essentially admitted under oath that USPS would bend the knee to Trump’s attacks on vote-by-mail. Sen. Peters: "Yes or no, if a state refuses to turn their absentee voter list over to the federal government, will the Postal Service still mail their ballots under this proposed rule?" Postmaster General David Steiner: "Under our proposed regulation, no." pic.twitter.com/4JYe7Jo450 — The Bulwark (@BulwarkOnline) June 24, 2026 However, sources familiar with Steiner’s plans told Reuters his discontent stretched back even further. The White House was making efforts to assuage Steiner since the end of last year, with donors even setting him up on a golf outing with Trump on one of his properties in Florida in December.

articles.title: 'Cannot go on!' Trump melts down after Federal Reserve defies his wishes
articles.description: President Donald Trump took to his Truth Social platform on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve agreed to a significant increase in interest rates — demanding that they do the opposite and make a massive cut instead. "Interest Rates in the United States should be 1%, or less, because we are the Best Credit in the World — BY FAR," wrote Trump. "Our Country is BOOMING with new Investment! If we stopped Trading with every country that we have a Deficit with, which is most of them, we would make, at least, 1.5 Trillion Dollars a year." "The word 'Deficit' is nothing more than a fancy word for LOSS," Trump continued. "We are 'carrying' almost every country in the World, and that cannot go on any longer. LOWER THE INTEREST RATES FOR THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, AND FAST!" Economists broadly agree that while reductions in interest rates make borrowing cheaper and boost employment in the short run, it can also drive a run of high inflation even higher. Increases to interest rates are one of the Fed's primary tools to tamp down inflation, which has been surging due to fuel shortages from the war in Iran. Trump has put intense pressure on the Fed, an independent body intended not to be influenced by political considerations, to cut interest rates to time a surge of economic activity when Republicans need a boost in the midterm elections.
